title.fa: اسلام «فطری» و نقد روحانیت‌ستیز نزد طالبوف: نامه‌هایی از تکفیر و حج
title.en: Talibov's 'natural' Islam and his quarrel with the clergy: letters on takfir and the hajj
title.nl: Talibovs 'natuurlijke' islam en zijn conflict met de geestelijkheid

summary.fa: طالبوف خود را مسلمان می‌دانست، اما می‌خواست احکام با زمان هماهنگ شود و از تکفیر شدنِ کتاب‌هایش و از شرایط حج گله داشت. این‌ها دیدگاه و گزارش شخصی اوست.
summary.en: Talibov considered himself a Muslim yet wanted rulings adapted to the times; his letters complain of being declared an unbeliever and describe disliked hajj conditions. These are his personal views and reports.
summary.nl: Talibov beschouwde zichzelf als moslim maar wilde dat regels met de tijd meegingen; zijn brieven bevatten klachten over takfir en over de hadj. Dit zijn zijn eigen opvattingen.

text.fa: در نامه‌ای می‌گوید اسلامش «طبیعی و فطری» است و کسی را به‌خاطر تکفیر او کافر نمی‌شمارد؛ به نظر او هر انسانِ یکتاپرست مسلمان حقیقی است.
text.en: In a letter he says his Islam is natural and innate and that he does not call his accusers unbelievers; in his view anyone who truly affirms one God is a real Muslim.
text.nl: In a letter he says his Islam is natural and innate and that he does not call his accusers unbelievers; in his view anyone who truly affirms one God is a real Muslim.

text.fa: به گفتهٔ افشار به نقل از کسروی، شیخ فضل‌الله نوری خواندن مسالک‌المحسنین را ممنوع و نویسنده را تکفیر کرده بود؛ طالبوف در نامه‌ای می‌نویسد اگر نوشته‌هایش بی‌معنا بود، علما تکفیرش نمی‌کردند.
text.en: Afshar, citing Kasravi, says Sheikh Fazlollah Nuri banned the reading of Masalek al-Mohsenin and declared its author an unbeliever; Talibov writes that if his texts were meaningless the clergy would not have excommunicated him.
text.nl: Afshar, citing Kasravi, says Sheikh Fazlollah Nuri banned the reading of Masalek al-Mohsenin and declared its author an unbeliever; Talibov writes that if his texts were meaningless the clergy would not have excommunicated him.

text.fa: از «علما» می‌خواهد با حفظ اسلام احکام را با مقتضیات زمان هماهنگ کنند و می‌گوید باید «سی هزار مسئله» به احکام افزود؛ تکفیر را سلاحی کهنه می‌داند که در برابر نوشته‌های ناآشنا به کار می‌برند.
text.en: He asks the clergy to adapt rulings to the times while preserving Islam, saying thirty thousand new questions must be added to the corpus, and calls takfir an old weapon used against unfamiliar writing.
text.nl: He asks the clergy to adapt rulings to the times while preserving Islam, saying thirty thousand new questions must be added to the corpus, and calls takfir an old weapon used against unfamiliar writing.

text.fa: در نامه‌ای دربارهٔ سفر حج خود سخت از شلوغی، پلشتی و رفتار حاجیان و مأموران می‌نالد، سفر حج را در آن زمان توصیه نمی‌کند و برای کعبه احترام معنوی قائل است؛ این‌ها مشاهدات و داوری شخصی یک مسافر در همان روزگار است و تعمیم‌های او دربارهٔ مردم حجاز را نمی‌توان معتبر دانست.
text.en: In a letter on his own hajj he complains harshly of crowding, filth and the conduct of pilgrims and officials, advises against going at that time, yet reveres the Kaaba spiritually; these are one traveller's impressions of his own day, and his sweeping remarks about the people of the Hijaz cannot be taken as reliable.
text.nl: In a letter on his own hajj he complains harshly of crowding, filth and the conduct of pilgrims and officials, advises against going at that time, yet reveres the Kaaba spiritually; these are one traveller's impressions of his own day, and his sweeping remarks about the people of the Hijaz cannot be taken as reliable.

text.fa: نظر رایج دانشگاهی: طالبوف را از روشنفکران اصلاح‌گرای مسلمان و پیشگام نثر نو می‌شمارند، و نقدهای تند او به برخی روحانیان و رفتارهای دینی در متن اختلاف شدید زمانهٔ مشروطه میان مشروطه‌خواهان و مشروعه‌خواهان بررسی می‌شود نه به‌عنوان داوری دربارهٔ دین به‌طور کلی.
text.en: Mainstream scholarly view: Talibov is treated as a reformist Muslim intellectual and pioneer of modern prose, and his sharp comments on some clerics are read within the heated Constitutional-era quarrel between constitutionalists and their clerical opponents, not as a verdict on religion as such.
text.nl: Mainstream scholarly view: Talibov is treated as a reformist Muslim intellectual and pioneer of modern prose, and his sharp comments on some clerics are read within the heated Constitutional-era quarrel between constitutionalists and their clerical opponents, not as a verdict on religion as such.
